vulnerability.title: Symfony X509Authenticator uses an unanchored emailAddress regex, allowing identity spoofing via a crafted certificate Subject DN

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.4.52 the emailAddress alternative is anchored to the start of the DN or a comma/slash boundary; fix 59ef4840 is an ancestor of the tag and absent from v5.4.45
Same tree: tag v5.4.52 peels to eabc5f9e and X509Authenticator.php blob 13e0c82b matches the patch post-image

fix_commits.message: [Security] Anchor emailAddress regex to RDN boundary in X509Authenticator

severity.numeric_level_rationale: CVSS 4.0 base 9.1 falls in Critical (9.0-10.0); the CNA and NVD (Secondary) both publish this vector with attack requirements present
severity.source: GitHub_M CNA CVSS 4.0 metric, also republished by NVD as its only, Secondary metric

vulnerability.category_l2: an unanchored emailAddress= regex matches inside the value of another RDN, so a certificate with a free-text CN can assert a victim email address

critical_operation.description: extractUsername falls back to parsing SSL_CLIENT_S_DN when SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email is absent. The regex looks for emailAddress= anywhere in the DN string and captures the following address. Because it is not anchored to an RDN boundary, a certificate whose CN value contains the text "emailAddress=victim@example.com" is parsed as that email address, and the captured value becomes the authenticated username. The 5.4.52 fix requires the match to start at the string start or after a comma or slash, and also accepts the dotted OID form.

entry_point.description: extractUsername() receives the Request built by the web server after it validated the client certificate and passed the Subject DN in SSL_CLIENT_S_DN. The DN is attacker-influenced only through the CA-issued certificate subject, so the attacker needs a certificate from a trusted CA whose CN accepts free text.

trace.description: The web server validates the client certificate and forwards its Subject DN as SSL_CLIENT_S_DN
With no SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email, the unanchored regex is applied to the whole DN string
The captured address is returned as the authenticated username

supports: extractUsername() reads SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email directly when present; otherwise it applies preg_match to SSL_CLIENT_S_DN
the pattern #emailAddress=([^,/@]++@[^,/]++)# is unanchored, so emailAddress= is recognized anywhere in the DN string, including inside the value of CN or another RDN
the captured address becomes the authenticated username without further canonicalization
the match must start at the beginning of the DN or after a comma or slash, so emailAddress= inside a CN value no longer matches
the RFC 4514 dotted OID form for emailAddress is accepted as well
the 5.4 patch changes exactly one line in X509Authenticator::extractUsername to anchor the emailAddress alternative to an RDN boundary
the patch adds a regression test covering a CN value that contains emailAddress=
the patch touches only X509Authenticator.php and X509AuthenticatorTest.php

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on CWE-290, the mechanism, the affected <5.4.52 range and the v5.4.52 release. The GHSA body and OSV reference name a nonexistent fix commit ccb3f724; the CNA reference 59ef4840 resolves, is dated 2026-04-17 and matches the advisory resolution. NVD carries only the CNA 4.0 9.1 vector as a Secondary metric. GHSA labels the issue HIGH while its 4.0 vector computes to 9.1 Critical; the canonical severity uses the published CNA/NVD 4.0 score.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read X509Authenticator::extractUsername at v5.4.45 and confirm the emailAddress regex is unanchored.
An independent reviewer must confirm 59ef4840 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.52 with the RDN-boundary anchor, and that ccb3f724 does not exist.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.52.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No mTLS stack, certificate or PHP runtime was executed; the finding is static.

The attacker model requires a certificate issued by a CA the web server trusts, with a CN that accepts the text "emailAddress=..." without encoding; the advisory asserts this is possible for some CAs but no specific CA was tested.
Only the 5.4 branch was fetched and compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
The GHSA body and OSV record name a dead fix commit ccb3f724; the dossier uses the resolvable CNA commit 59ef4840.
GHSA severity HIGH and the 4.0 vector score 9.1 Critical disagree; the canonical severity keeps the published 4.0 vector and records the label difference.
open_questions: Which CAs allow an unescaped emailAddress= sequence inside a CN value was not surveyed.
Whether the web server passes a normalized or raw DN representation was not tested.
